Word for Mac executive assistant templates
intro: Word for executive assistants on Mac comes down to four jobs: reusable templates, AutoText snippets, Track Changes for manager review, and mail merge. Mac Word leaves out some Windows features, so the Mac workarounds matter. Lazur can point at the right button and guide you through each step.
tldr: Build agendas, briefing notes and itineraries as templates. Save them from File > Save as Template.
Mac Word has no Quick Parts. Use AutoText for the snippets you reuse every week.
Keep master templates in a local folder. Templates on network locations can fail on Mac.
Mac Word does not embed fonts. Send a PDF when the layout must stay fixed.
Lazur points at buttons, guides you one click at a time and dictates with fn. It never clicks for you.

blocks.text: Most executive assistants use Word for four jobs. They rebuild the same documents, keep standard text on hand, mark up drafts from a manager, and send one letter to many people. Word for Mac handles all four. It also leaves out some Windows features, so you need the Mac way of doing each job.
Templates for agendas, briefing notes and itineraries

A template is a saved document with the layout already set. Agendas, briefing notes, travel itineraries and handover documents are good first candidates. Each one has headings, a standard table and fields you refill every time. Build the shell once, then open a fresh copy when you need it.
Keep the template to structure only. Leave out names, dates and figures. If a manager's name lives in the master file, you will send the wrong name sooner or later.
Save a Word template on Mac
Start with a finished layout, not a blank page. Set your styles, headers, footers and placeholder text first. Then save it.

items: Choose File > Save as Template.
Type a name that says what the file is, such as Weekly leadership agenda.
Pick the file format. Use Word Template (.dotx) for most files. Use Macro-Enabled (.dotm) only if the file contains macros.
Click Save. Open a new copy later with File > New from Template.

blocks.text: Where Mac Word keeps templates

Word for Mac keeps templates in a folder inside your user Group Containers. The default path is /Users/your-username/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/User Content/Templates. To reach it fast, press ⇧⌘G in Finder and paste the path.

You can point Word at a different folder. Go to Word > Preferences > Personal Settings > File Locations, then change User templates. Microsoft's page says deleting a template happens in Finder, so move the file to the Trash from there.
Network templates on Mac and what to do instead

Many offices keep master templates on a shared drive. On Mac, that setup is unreliable. A Word MVP reference lists several path-resolution bugs for templates in network locations. It recommends copying the template to the Mac's My Templates folder.

Pick one person as the owner of each master file. Give the file a clear name, such as Board agenda final, so nobody opens an old copy. When the master changes, copy the new version to each Mac by hand.
AutoText, the Mac version of Quick Parts

If you searched for Quick Parts on Mac, here is the short answer. Quick Parts and Building Blocks are a Word for Windows feature that Mac does not have. Microsoft 365 for Mac uses AutoText for the same job. That answer comes from a Microsoft Q&A thread, so check behavior on your own build.

A volunteer moderator in that thread said AutoText entries saved on Windows also work on the Mac. That helps if your office keeps a shared set of snippets. Test one entry on a Mac before you rely on it.
Build a snippet you type every week

Pick text you retype often. Good candidates are the dial-in line for a standing call, your office address block, or a polite line about a late reply. Select the text, find AutoText under Insert > AutoText, and save it under a short name.
Insert it again from the same menu. Keep names short, and avoid names that match real words. Review the list every few months, because old snippets with old phone numbers cause real trouble.
Track Changes and comments for manager review on Mac

When a manager sends back a draft, you need to see every edit. Turn on Track Changes from Review > Track Changes, or press ⌘⇧E. Each edit then shows in color, with the author name beside it. Accept or reject each change once you have checked it.
Use comments for questions, not for edits. Select the text and press ⌥⌘A to insert a comment. The manager can answer in the margin without touching the wording.
Track Changes mistakes that cost time

items: Leaving Track Changes on when you send a clean copy. The next reader sees every stray edit.
Accepting all changes at once. Read each one first, especially names, dates and amounts.
Sending a file with tracked changes to someone outside the company without a clean copy.
Forgetting your name on the markup. Check your name in Word preferences before a long review.

blocks.text: Mail merge in Word on Mac for letters, labels and invitations
Mail merge fills a letter or label with rows from a list. Use it when one letter goes to a long guest list, or when each vendor needs the same notice with a different name and date.

Start in Mailings > Start Mail Merge and pick the document type. Then choose the recipient list. Keep the list in a spreadsheet with one column per field, such as first name, company and reply date. Insert the merge fields where the names belong, then preview before you print.
Test with a few rows first. Check dates, accented letters and line breaks. Save the merged result as a new file so the template stays clean.
Fonts, ribbons and macros that do not travel well

Many executives send files between a Mac and a Windows PC. Some things do not carry over cleanly. A Word MVP reference says font embedding is not supported on Mac. Recipients need the same fonts installed, or Word will substitute a different one.

Ribbon customizations are also a Mac gap. The same reference says ribbon changes are silently ignored on Mac Word, although toolbars can still be customized. Spend your time on keyboard shortcuts and templates instead of a custom ribbon.

Macros are weaker too. The reference says Mac VBA is version 6, roughly Word 2000 level, while Windows Word 2013 uses version 7. ActiveX is not supported at all. The page has no date, so treat its details as a starting point.
A quick check before you send a file

items: Export a PDF for anything that must look exact.
Confirm the recipient has every font in the document, or send the PDF instead.
Turn off Track Changes and check the comments pane for leftover notes.
Open the file once in a new window to confirm links and fields still work.

blocks.text: Language changes can reset your Normal template

This one catches people off guard. If you switch the primary language in System Settings, Word creates a new default template. It renames your old Normal.dotm to a numbered copy, so your custom styles seem to vanish.
To restore the old file, quit Word and replace the new Normal.dotm with the old one. Before you change languages, copy your Templates folder. That takes a minute and saves a long afternoon.
Copilot in Word for first drafts

Copilot in Word can draft text, rewrite a paragraph and summarize a long document. Microsoft says most of its 84 million consumer subscribers will have access to Copilot in Word. Personal and Family subscribers also receive a monthly allotment of AI credits.

Microsoft says that allotment should be enough for most subscribers, but it does not publish a credit number. Check your own account before you plan a heavy week. Don't rely on a figure from a blog post.
How much Word work takes, and what the numbers do not say
No study of executive assistant time in Word was found. The figures below cover office workers and managers in general. Treat them as context, not as a measure of your week.

Zapier surveyed 1,000 people who work at or own small and medium-sized businesses. Of those, 83% said they spend 1 to 3 hours a day fixing errors. Zapier does not give a survey date, so read the figure as a rough signal.

Nitro surveyed 239 C-suite executives and 1,100 managers and directors in the US, UK and Canada. 62% of managers say their team spends 6+ hours a week on manual document processing. Those are perceptions of other people's time, not time logs.
The useful takeaway is simple. Document work is repetitive, and the people who do it feel it. Templates, AutoText and mail merge cut the repeat work, even though no one has measured your exact hours.
Where Lazur fits inside Word

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on your screen, and Lazur answers out loud. It sees the Word window only while you hold the shortcut. It does not click buttons, edit your file or act as a plugin.

Ask where something is and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. That suits Word, where one task can sit under several tabs and menus.

Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Dictation works well for a briefing note you talk through on the way back from a meeting. Check names and figures before you send. Speech tools can miss a proper noun.
Snippets and a personal dictionary for names

Lazur keeps snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots for dictation. Add the names you type every week, such as board members, venue contacts and your manager's title. That gives dictation a head start on those names.
Lazur also keeps a memory of what you asked and did, stored on the Mac. That helps when you return to a template a week later and forget a step.
What Lazur sends out and what it keeps

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer. They are not stored there, and content is never used to train AI models.
Still, read your office rules before you point any voice assistant at confidential board material. Lazur does not replace that check, and your company policy comes first.
Worked example: a weekly leadership agenda template
Here is one full example. You support a leadership team that meets every week. The agenda needs the same sections each time, a running list of open actions and a time box for each item.

items: Open a blank document. Add the meeting title, a date field and the attendee line.
Add the standing sections as headings: wins, numbers, decisions and open actions.
Insert a table for actions with columns for owner, task and due date.
Apply one body style to all text, and check that the headings show in the navigation pane.
Choose File > Save as Template and name it Weekly leadership agenda.
Open a new copy each week with File > New from Template, then fill in the blanks.

blocks.text: The first copy takes the longest. After that, each week takes a few minutes. If you forget a step, ask Lazur to walk you through it, such as how to set a heading style.
Mistakes executive assistants make in Word on Mac

items: Saving a master template to a shared drive and assuming it opens for everyone.
Following a Windows guide that says Quick Parts. The Mac uses AutoText.
Sending the .docx to someone without the fonts. Export a PDF for a final copy.
Building macros for a workflow that belongs on a Windows machine.
Keeping several copies of the same template. Versions drift apart quickly.

blocks.text: Most of these mistakes are cheap to fix once you know them. They usually cost you time later, in the meeting, not in the moment you make them.
Keeping Word for Mac current

Microsoft lists Word for Mac builds in its release notes. The latest Word entry in those notes is 16.114.3, dated Oct 27, 2026, with build 26102720. The October 2026 Word entries say only quality and performance improvements.
Check your version with Word > About Word. If your number is lower, update before you rely on a feature. Microsoft's release notes are the source to check, not a blog post.
What to do next

Pick one template this week. Start with the agenda or the travel itinerary, since you reuse both. Then add one AutoText snippet and one Track Changes habit. Small steps stick better than a full rebuild.

For more on Word on Mac with a voice helper, read [Word on Mac with Lazur](/apps/word). If your work also runs through mail, the [Outlook guide for executive assistants](/for/executive-assistants/outlook) covers delegates and calendars.

faq.question: Does Word for Mac have Quick Parts?
faq.answer: No. Microsoft says Building Blocks and Quick Parts are a Word for Windows feature. Microsoft 365 for Mac uses AutoText for reusable text. A volunteer moderator in the same thread said AutoText entries saved on Windows also work on the Mac.

faq.question: Where does Word for Mac save templates?
faq.answer: By default, Word saves them in your user Group Containers folder, in the UBF8T346G9.Office User Content Templates folder. To change it, go to Word > Preferences > Personal Settings > File Locations and edit User templates.

faq.question: Can I open a template from a shared network drive on a Mac?
faq.answer: You can, but it is unreliable. A Word MVP reference cites several path-resolution bugs for network templates on Mac. Copy the master template to your Mac's My Templates folder, and update the copy by hand when the master changes.

faq.question: Do fonts travel with a Word file from a Mac?
faq.answer: Not reliably. Font embedding is not supported on Mac, so recipients need the same fonts installed. Send a PDF when the layout must stay fixed.

faq.question: Does Lazur edit my Word document for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points, guides, answers out loud, dictates and drafts text. It does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. You make the change yourself.

faq.question: Which version of Word for Mac should I have?
faq.answer: The latest Word entry in Microsoft's Office for Mac release notes is 16.114.3, dated Oct 27, 2026. Check your version under Word > About Word, and update if your number is lower.

faq.question: Is Copilot in Word included with my subscription?
faq.answer: Microsoft says most of its 84 million consumer subscribers will have access to Copilot in Word. Personal and Family plans include a monthly allotment of AI credits, but Microsoft does not publish a number. Check your own account.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with Word on Windows?
faq.answer: Lazur is for the Mac, on Apple silicon and Intel. Windows is planned, not available yet. On the Mac, Lazur works from the notch while you keep Word open.
